title: Storage, Scrambling, and Loss of Information in Quantum Reservoir Computing
summary: The performance of a quantum reservoir computer in temporal processing tasks depends on how its driven quantum substrate retains information about past inputs, distributes it across physical degrees of freedom, and loses it through environmental dissipation and measurement feedback. We formulate these processes using a classical-quantum state obtained by restricting a reservoir process tensor to classical input encoding and single-time readout.
